leading_positions.synthesis: Four members put targeted protein degradation in their round-1 configuration; three of them (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski) name Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with PROTAC-centred citations, while Linke names only Crews and Deshaies as one part of a two-part prize. All four describe induced proximity to an E3 ligase and cite independent confirmation. They do not share a view on Ciulli, on whether the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) belongs in or beside the citation, or on whether clinical maturity is sufficient; Aqvist and Brzezinski ranked it first only after reading colleagues' opening ballots. Somfai, Chabes and Zou list it only as an alternative (Somfai, Zou) or a second alternative (Chabes).

Three members include base editing in their configuration. Chabes proposes Liu, Komor and Gaudelli as the sole prize; Linke and Somfai propose Liu alone, in each case as one part of a two-part prize (with B028 for Linke, with B008 for Somfai). They share the view that the deamination chemistry is distinct from Cas9 cleavage and independently reproduced. They differ on whether Komor and Gaudelli should be credited, and none of the three configurations includes Kondo and Nishida. Chabes and Linke have each moved or confirmed positions in response to the attribution objection raised by Somfai, Zou and Aqvist; Aili and Aqvist list B061 only as an alternative and Brzezinski lists it as a second alternative.

Somfai and Zou both name Buchwald and Hartwig for Pd-catalysed C-N coupling, Zou as the whole prize and Somfai as one part paired with B061 (and noting that B008 should stand alone if B061 is not accepted). They agree that Kosugi's tin-amide work is a precursor, that the catalytic ligand-controlled method is the achievement, and that the 2010 prize did not cover amination. Their citations differ slightly: Somfai's stresses ligand design; Zou's names only C-N coupling. Linke names B008 as a first alternative and would support it as a companion part; Chabes, Aili, Aqvist and Brzezinski do not mention it as a preferred or alternative ballot in their configurations.

Only Sparr names biomolecular phase separation (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen) in her configuration, as a physical-chemical principle of cellular organisation. Her own case against concedes that the generality of in-cell liquid-liquid phase separation is still debated and that Pappu and Mittag are left out. Aili ranks it third and Linke lists it as a second alternative, but neither places it in a preferred configuration.

areas_of_agreement: All eight members explicitly describe targeted protein degradation (B028) as scientifically serious and mechanistically confirmed; four place it in their preferred configuration and Somfai, Zou and Sparr name it as an alternative. Disagreement concerns timing and attribution, not whether the chemistry is real.
Members across B061, B028 and B008 agree that the Kosugi tin-amide work is a precursor and not a co-laureate for C-N coupling, and that the 2010 cross-coupling prize did not cover amination.

Members agree that the Car-Parrinello candidacy (B037) has the cleanest attribution (Car and Parrinello) and long validation, and that the Gray and Winkler candidacy (B055) has a clean attribution; each is the preferred choice only in the opening of one member, and no one else includes either in a preferred configuration.

Most members who discuss base editing (Chabes, Linke, Somfai, Aqvist, Zou) agree that the Komor and Gaudelli contributions are real, with the open point being how a prize should treat them, and that long-term clinical safety is not fully established.
scientific_disputes: Whether base editing (B061) is a distinct chemical achievement (deamination of a displaced strand, no double-strand break) or an engineering refinement of the platform recognised in 2020 (Chabes and Linke versus Sparr, Zou and, in part, Aili and Aqvist).

Whether C-N coupling (B008) is a new mechanistic achievement (Somfai, Zou, with Zou arguing that C-N reductive elimination needed a different solution) or an extension of the 2010 prize (a concern raised by Somfai himself, Aqvist, Chabes and Aili).
Whether in-cell biomolecular condensates (B015) reflect a general demixing principle or one still debated on methodological grounds (Sparr, Aili, Linke).

Whether a computational method such as Car-Parrinello dynamics (B037) is chemistry in the statutory sense and has chemical uptake beyond condensed-matter physics (Brzezinski, Somfai), and whether the committee wants computation represented this year.
Whether the new element in Gray and Winkler's electron-transfer work (B055) goes beyond the 1992 Marcus prize (Aqvist, Sparr).
attribution_disputes: B028: Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli (Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski) versus Crews and Deshaies only (Linke) versus a Handa-for-Ciulli swap (raised by Chabes in his ballot and discussed by Aili); the cereblon glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) may require separate recognition or a different configuration, and at least Aili, Aqvist, Brzezinski and Somfai flag this.

B061: Liu, Komor and Gaudelli (Chabes) versus Liu alone (Linke, Somfai, and Aqvist and Zou in their discussion); Kondo and Nishida (Target-AID) are included in no preferred configuration, and Chabes, Linke and Somfai each flag the parallel work as a gap.
B008: Buchwald and Hartwig are named by both supporters; the only attribution question raised is Kosugi and Migita, which both Somfai and Zou treat as a precursor.
B015: Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen versus including Pappu and Mittag for sequence-encoded theory (Sparr, Linke).
maturity_disputes: B028: Aili says the mechanism is confirmed and human proof of concept exists; Aqvist, Brzezinski, Somfai, Chabes and Zou say clinical validation is still accumulating and that no approved PROTAC drug is established to their knowledge. Aqvist asks whether mechanism confirmation alone justifies recognition now.

B061: field is about ten years old and the clinical record, off-target and bystander-editing data are short (Chabes, Brzezinski, Somfai, Linke), set against independent reproduction and patients already treated (Chabes, Aili, Linke).
B015: debate over the physiological extent of liquid-liquid phase separation is unresolved, and Sparr and Aili both suggest revisiting it in a few years.
B008, B037 and B055: no maturity concern is raised by any member; the objections concern novelty and field, not maturity.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Linke (chair) is a Lund colleague of Somfai and Sparr; Somfai and Sparr each disclose the same Lund overlap. Linke states none of the shortlisted candidates is at Lund or a known collaborator, and no recusal is requested.

Brzezinski discloses that his field (proton and electron transfer in respiratory enzymes) is close to B055, his own opening first choice, and is a Stockholm University colleague of Zou; neither is in his preferred configuration or alternatives. He flags a possible bias, no recusal.
Aqvist discloses a postdoc with Warshel and closeness to computational candidacies B037 and B001, with no direct collaboration with candidates; he does not think recusal is needed.
Somfai discloses that his mentor Masamune was at MIT, where Buchwald works, with no direct tie to any candidate.

Chabes and Sparr each disclose a field adjacent to a candidacy (DNA repair and dNTP pools next to base editing; lipid-protein co-assembly and amyloid next to condensates) without a personal or institutional tie. Aili and Zou state no conflict and Zou says she defers on chemical biology candidates.
questions_for_round2: B028: Should the citation cover PROTACs only (Crews and Deshaies, with or without Ciulli), or must the cereblon molecular-glue strand (Handa, Ito, Gray) be recognised, either in the same part or as a separate part? If Ciulli and Handa compete for a third place, what criterion decides between them?

B028: How much weight should the absence of an approved PROTAC drug carry, given the argument that the criterion is a discovery of great benefit and not an approval count? Would members who cite maturity (Aqvist, Brzezinski, Somfai) support B028 if the citation is explicitly limited to the mechanism and design principle?

B061: Is Liu alone the defensible configuration, or Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, and how should the committee handle Kondo and Nishida's parallel Target-AID work? Can members state what is new chemically, beyond deaminase chemistry, in the cytosine and adenine editors separately?

B061 against B028: Given proximity to the 2020 prize for B061 and the absence of any previous recognition of degradation, can the committee compare these on the criteria that members themselves have raised (attribution clarity, novelty relative to prior prizes, and maturity)?

B008: Does the 2010 prize make C-N coupling a repetition, or is the distinct ligand-design and C-N reductive-elimination problem sufficient? Would Somfai and Zou accept B008 as a stand-alone two-laureate prize if B061 is not carried, and would others support it as a companion part?

Two-part prizes: Are the paired configurations (B061 with B028, B061 with B008) acceptable within the three-laureate limit, or should the committee first decide which single candidacy can reach five votes? Which members would move to a single-part prize?

B037, B055 and B015: Does any member wish to advocate for these, and if so, what specific evidence (chemical uptake of Car-Parrinello methods, what the Gray work adds beyond 1992, the extent of physiological phase separation) would justify a place in round 2 beside B028, B061 and B008?
summary.chair_observation: In round 1, B028 is explicitly in four configurations, B061 in three and B008 in two, with B015 in one, and two members propose two-part prizes. Positions on attribution within B028 and B061 are not aligned even among supporters, and maturity and closeness to earlier prizes are the main objections raised against both. No candidacy has the five explicit supporters needed for a majority on the face of the round-1 files, so round 2 needs to resolve configuration questions before the final ballot. As chair I also hold a stated preference (B061 with B028) and note that my counts come only from explicit positions in the eight files.
